column1: In general, it is plausible to suppose that we should prefer peace and quiet to noise.
column2: 一般说来，有理由认为，相比噪声，我们更喜欢平静安宁。

column1: And yet most of us have had the experience of having to adjust to sleeping in the mountains or the countryside because it was initially ‘too quiet’, an experience that suggests that humans are capable of adapting to a wide range of noise levels.
column2: 可我们大多有过这样的经历：在山区或乡下睡觉，一开始觉得“太安静”，得花些时间适应。这表明人能适应相差很大的噪声水平。
column3: most of us|我们大多数人
column10: a wide range of|范围很广的

column1: Research supports this view.
column2: 研究支持这一观点。

column1: For example, Glass and Singer (1972) exposed people to short bursts of very loud noise and then measured their ability to work out problems and their physiological reactions to the noise.
column2: 例如，Glass和Singer（1972）让受试者短暂暴露于极其喧闹的噪音中，随后测量他们解决问题的能力及对噪音的生理反应。

column1: The noise was quite disruptive at first, but after about four minutes the subjects were doing just as well on their tasks as control subjects who were not exposed to noise.
column2: 噪音起初很干扰人，但大约四分钟后，受试者的任务表现与未接触噪音的对照组相当。

column1: Their physiological arousal also declined quickly to the same levels as those of the control subjects.
column2: 他们的生理唤醒水平也迅速下降，达到对照组的相同水平。

column1: But there are limits to adaptation and loud noise becomes more troublesome if the person is required to concentrate on more than one task.
column2: 不过，人的适应能力有限。如果一个人需要同时专注于不止一项任务，响亮的噪声就会更扰人。
column9: more than one task|不止一项任务

column1: For example, high noise levels interfered with the performance of subjects who were required to monitor three dials at a time, a task not unlike that of an aeroplane pilot or an air-traffic controller (Broadbent, 1957).
column2: 例如，受试者需要同时监看三个仪表盘时，强噪声会影响他们的表现。这项任务颇似飞行员或空中交通管制员的工作（布罗德本特，1957年）。
column13: air-traffic controller|n. 空中交通管制员

column1: Similarly, noise did not affect a subject’s ability to track a moving line with a steering wheel, but it did interfere with the subject’s ability to repeat numbers while tracking (Finkelman and Glass, 1970).
column2: 同样，噪声并不影响受试者用方向盘追踪移动线条的能力，但如果要一边追踪一边复述数字，噪声确实会干扰他们复述数字的能力（芬克尔曼和格拉斯，1970年）。

column1: Probably the most significant finding from research on noise is that its predictability is more important than how loud it is.
column2: 噪音研究中最重要的一项发现是：其可预测性比声音大小更重要。

column1: We are much more able to ‘tune out’ chronic background noise, even if it is quite loud, than to work under circumstances with unexpected intrusions of noise.
column2: 持续的背景噪声，即使相当响，我们也比较容易把它“屏蔽”掉。相比之下，要在不时受到突发噪声干扰的环境中工作，就难得多了。
column9: unexpected intrusions of noise|突发的噪声干扰

column1: In the Glass and Singer study, in which subjects were exposed to bursts of noise as they worked on a task, some subjects heard loud bursts and others heard soft bursts.
column2: 在格拉斯和辛格的研究中，受试者在完成任务时听到一阵阵噪声。有些人听到的噪声很响，有些人听到的则很轻。
column6: bursts of noise|n. 一阵阵噪声
column7: worked on a task|执行一项任务
column8: loud bursts|n. 一阵阵响亮的噪声
column9: soft bursts|n. 一阵阵轻微的噪声

column1: For some subjects, the bursts were spaced exactly one minute apart (predictable noise); others heard the same amount of noise overall, but the bursts occurred at random intervals (unpredictable noise).
column2: 有些受试者听到的一阵阵噪声恰好相隔一分钟（可预测噪声）。另一些人听到的噪声总量相同，但各阵噪声之间的间隔是随机的（不可预测噪声）。
column10: at random intervals|以随机的时间间隔
column11: unpredictable noise|n. 不可预测噪声

column1: Subjects reported finding the predictable and unpredictable noise equally annoying, and all subjects performed at about the same level during the noise portion of the experiment.
column2: 受试者表示，可预测和不可预测的噪音同样令人烦恼；在实验的噪音阶段，所有受试者的表现水平相当。

column1: But the different noise conditions had quite different after-effects when the subjects were required to proofread written material under conditions of no noise.
column2: 然而，当受试者在无噪音环境下校对书面材料时，不同噪音条件产生了截然不同的后续效应。

column1: As shown in Table 1 the unpredictable noise produced more errors in the later proofreading task than predictable noise; and soft, unpredictable noise actually produced slightly more errors on this task than the loud, predictable noise.
column2: 如表1所示，不可预测的噪声在后续校对任务中导致的错误比可预测的噪声更多；而柔和的不可预测噪声在此任务中产生的错误，甚至略多于响亮的可预测噪声。

column1: Apparently, unpredictable noise produces more fatigue than predictable noise, but it takes a while for this fatigue to take its toll on performance.
column2: 显然，不可预测的噪音比可预测的噪音更容易导致疲劳，不过这种疲劳对性能的影响需要一段时间才会显现出来。

column1: Predictability is not the only variable that reduces or eliminates the negative effects of noise.
column2: 可预测性并不是唯一能够减少或消除噪声负面影响的因素。

column1: Another is control.
column2: 另一个是控制。

column1: If the individual knows that he or she can control the noise, this seems to eliminate both its negative effects at the time and its after-effects.
column2: 如果一个人知道自己能够控制噪声，那么，噪声当时的不利影响和事后的影响似乎都会消失。

column1: This is true even if the individual never actually exercises his or her option to turn the noise off (Glass and Singer, 1972).
column2: 即使个人实际上从未行使过关闭噪音的选项，这种情况仍然成立（Glass和Singer，1972年）。

column1: Just the knowledge that one has control is sufficient.
column2: 仅仅知道拥有控制权就足够了。

column1: The studies discussed so far exposed people to noise for only short periods and only transient effects were studied.
column2: 迄今为止所进行的研究都仅让参与者短暂地接触噪音，因此所研究的都是一些短暂的影响而已。

column1: But the major worry about noisy environments is that living day after day with chronic noise may produce serious, lasting effects.
column2: 但是，对嘈杂环境的主要担忧是：长期生活在这样的环境中可能会带来严重的、持久的影响。

column1: One study, suggesting that this worry is a realistic one, compared elementary school pupils who attended schools near Los Angeles’s busiest airport with students who attended schools in quiet neighbourhoods (Cohen et al., 1980).
column2: 一项研究表明，这种担忧确有根据。研究者比较了两组小学生：一组在洛杉矶最繁忙的机场附近上学，另一组在安静的街区上学（科恩等，1980年）。

column1: It was found that children from the noisy schools had higher blood pressure and were more easily distracted than those who attended the quiet schools.
column2: 研究发现，与在安静学校上学的儿童相比，在嘈杂学校上学的儿童血压更高，也更容易分心。
column5: higher blood pressure|n. 较高的血压

column1: Moreover, there was no evidence of adaptability to the noise.
column2: 此外，也没有证据表明这些儿童能够适应这种噪音环境。

column1: In fact, the longer the children had attended the noisy schools, the more distractible they became.
column2: 事实上，孩子们在嘈杂学校就读的时间越长，他们的注意力就越难以集中。

column1: The effects also seem to be long lasting.
column2: 这些效果似乎也相当持久。

column1: A follow-up study showed that children who were moved to less noisy classrooms still showed greater distractibility one year later than students who had always been in the quiet schools (Cohen et al, 1981).
column2: 一项后续研究指出，那些被转至噪音较小的教室里的孩子，在一年后仍然表现出更高的注意力分散现象，这一点与一直就读于安静教室的学生相比更为明显（Cohen等人，1981年）。

column1: It should be noted that the two groups of children had been carefully matched by the investigators so that they were comparable in age, ethnicity, race, and social class.
column2: 需要注意的是，这两组儿童经过了仔细的匹配，以确保他们在年龄、族裔、种族和社会阶级方面具有可比性。
